scope: Independent verifier, persistent synthetic provider, role credential separation, contract lifecycle tests and repeatability tooling
changes: Purchasing services load participant credentials only and request outcomes from a separate authenticated verifier process.
The verifier independently reads ledger and provider evidence and checks exact purchase bindings before signing an outcome.
Purchasing services independently read the terminal ledger state; an HTTP success claim alone cannot release a hold.
A separate SQLite-backed MOCK provider retains orders and capture evidence across process restarts, with distinct dispatch and read tokens.
The app demo retains private role configurations, keys, databases, provider-call assertions and HTTP latency under .boundpay-runs.
Persistent setup builds matching Drunix CLI tools offline from the vendored pinned v1.0.0 source in a digest-pinned Go container.
A repeatability runner alternates timeout and response loss, saves each result, and summarizes route latency after all assertions pass.
New contract lifecycle tests exercise dispatch, unknown holds, exact identities, terminal outcome idempotency and prospective revocation.

jev_final_review.response: Added boundary rejection, process restart, read-only credential and independent ledger-readback tests; retained holds on uncertain evidence

limits: Fresh ledger-backed app demo and repeated ledger measurements were not executed for this upgrade; the preparation check does not start a network or deploy the contract.
The contract test fixture does not establish endorsement or MVCC behavior.
Processes share one host operator; separate configured credentials do not prove OS isolation or independent organizational governance.
Live model and Razorpay calls were not repeated. Razorpay payment failure alone is not accepted as terminal order failure by the new verifier.
The one locally mitigated braces development advisory remains recorded in the initial verification artifact.
Temporary verification logs may be removed by host cleanup.
